description:
You’ve probably heard that computers run on binary, 1s and 0s. But inside a computer, there aren’t any actual 1s and 0s moving around, so what does binary physically mean?

When we zoom into a CPU, we find billions of transistors connected by a maze of tiny metal wires. Running between them are power and ground rails. The power rail sits at roughly 0.7 to 1.3 volts and represents a 1. The ground rail sits at 0 volts and represents a 0. As transistors switch on and off, each logic gate’s output connects to either the power rail or the ground rail. That’s how voltage becomes the 1s and 0s behind everything your computer does.
